questions.question: The load-shedding years taught that the fastest relief for a strained electricity system is:
options: Trimming and shifting demand, which works within months, rather than a new station that takes a decade
Importing electricity from Europe
Building a new coal station within a year
Rationing electricity to households only

questions.question: Carbon border taxes pressure South Africa's energy management because:
options: They tax coal mines directly at the pit head
Imports manufactured with dirty electricity pay penalties at foreign borders, adding a surcharge to exported steel, wine and citrus
They fund new coal stations abroad
They apply only to electricity exports

questions.question: A greener economy is defined as one that:
options: Stops all industrial growth to cut emissions
Exports its polluting industries to neighbours
Keeps growing while its resource consumption and emissions fall — prosperity unhooked from pollution
Replaces farming with forestry

questions.question: Energy efficiency is nicknamed the invisible power station because:
options: Efficient appliances generate their own power
It refers to underground pumped storage plants
Efficiency only works at night when nobody sees it
Deleting a station's worth of demand is faster, cheaper and cleaner than building one, and it never emits a gram

questions.question: The Integrated Resource Plan is best described as:
options: The official electricity roadmap scheduling which coal stations retire and how much solar, wind, storage, gas and nuclear is procured by which year
A tax on industrial electricity users
The rulebook for appliance labelling
A register of household solar installations

questions.question: South Africa's carbon tax manages energy by:
options: Paying households to install geyser timers
Charging emitters per tonne of carbon dioxide so that pollution finally carries a price, nudging industry toward cleaner processes
Banning coal exports outright
Fixing the price of petrol nationwide

questions.question: Two quiet rules that save large amounts of energy are:
options: Speed limits and import quotas
Water restrictions and fishing permits
Building regulations requiring energy performance in new buildings, and compulsory appliance labels revealing running costs before purchase
Advertising codes and municipal bylaws on signage

questions.question: The Just Energy Transition Partnership channels international finance into:
options: Extending the life of the oldest coal stations
Subsidising petrol prices for commuters
Buying electricity from neighbouring countries
New transmission lines, retraining for coal-dependent towns and green manufacturing

questions.question: An energy audit is:
options: A methodical, metered trace of where a firm's energy actually goes — finding leaks, worn motors and wasted heat — with every fix ranked by payback
A government inspection that fines firms for high bills
An annual reading of the electricity meter
A stocktake of diesel generators

questions.question: Wheeling allows a company to:
options: Transport coal by road instead of rail
Produce electricity at a windy or sunny site and consume it, delivered across the public grid, at operations far away
Sell diesel to neighbouring firms
Rotate its machinery to cut friction losses

questions.question: A product's carbon footprint has become a passport to markets because:
options: Customers prefer heavier products
It qualifies firms for local tax rebates only
European border rules will tax embedded emissions, and lenders and buyers screen for climate risk before committing
It replaces quality certification entirely

questions.question: Greenwashing is:
options: Cleaning solar panels to keep output high
Recycling water inside a factory
Painting wind turbine blades green for visibility
Marketing an unchanged, polluting operation as eco-friendly instead of doing measurable energy management

questions.question: The geyser ladder, in order, is:
options: Thermostat down to sixty degrees, insulate the tank and pipes, fit a timer, then hand the job to a solar water heater or heat pump
Replace the geyser first, then insulate whatever remains
Switch the geyser off permanently and boil kettles
Raise the thermostat so the water stays hot longer

questions.question: Swapping filament bulbs for LEDs is called the cheapest win because an LED:
options: Is free to buy under national regulations
Gives the same light for roughly a tenth of the electricity and lasts for years
Generates a small surplus of electricity
Only works during load-shedding

questions.question: Standby power deserves attention because:
options: It powers the geyser during the night
It protects appliances from lightning
The ring of little red lights sips electricity all night while delivering nothing — the wall switch ends it
It only affects businesses, not homes

questions.question: The citizen layer of household energy management includes:
options: Reporting neighbours who use electricity at peak times
Refusing to pay municipal electricity bills
Reading the meter weekly for the utility
Shifting chores off the evening peak, turning the roof into a micro power station, and voicing support for the lines, plants and plans the transition needs

questions.question: In the leaking bucket picture, the holes are:
options: Wasteful losses like draughty buildings, filament bulbs, naked geysers, worn motors and offices lit for nobody
Power stations that burn too little coal
Illegal connections to the grid
Rivers evaporating from hydro dams

questions.question: Plugging holes beats building another dam because efficiency:
options: Requires no maintenance ever again
Costs a small fraction of a station's hundreds of billions, starts working within months, and emits nothing
Is paid for entirely by foreign donors
Doubles the output of existing stations

questions.question: The champion sentence of the whole topic is:
options: The grid is only as strong as its oldest station
Coal remains king until the seams run dry
The unit of electricity you never use is the cheapest and cleanest unit there is
Every home should go entirely off-grid

questions.question: The government spanner is the heavy one because only government can:
options: Rewrite the rules of the game — the IRP roadmap, renewable auctions, the carbon tax, building rules, appliance labels and the just-transition money
Install solar panels on private factory roofs
Conduct energy audits inside private firms
Choose which appliances households buy

questions.question: The clever firm starts with an energy audit, which hunts for:
options: Competitors' electricity prices
Waste in the plant — hissing air hoses, ancient motors, bare steam pipes — with fixes that pay for themselves
Employees arriving late for shifts
Errors in the municipal bill only

questions.question: The decade's new trade rule on the business spanner says:
options: Exports must travel by rail to qualify for rebates
All products need bilingual labels
Overseas buyers now ask how much smoke is inside your product, so a dirty grid has become a sales problem
Firms must export before selling locally

questions.question: The individual spanner matters despite being smallest because:
options: It is made of the strongest material
Individuals pay the highest tariffs
It is the only spanner that never breaks
Sixty million hands hold copies of it, all reaching for the same few bolts at home

questions.question: The evening peak is best described as:
options: Millions of private decisions — geysers, stoves, heaters, kettles — landing on the grid in the same hour
The moment power stations produce their maximum
A fault that occurs in transmission lines at dusk
The hour when electricity is cheapest

questions.question: Ranked by size, the first play a household should run is:
options: Unplugging the television at the wall
The geyser — around 40 per cent of the bill: thermostat down, blanket on, timer fitted, and solar if the family can stretch to it
Replacing the refrigerator every year
Cooking outdoors in summer

questions.question: The honest caveat that earns credit in an evaluation answer is:
options: Households cause most of South Africa's emissions
Individual changes make no difference and can be ignored
No single household can decarbonise a coal grid — but the peak is the sum of household choices, and the sum responds when millions adjust
Only businesses can influence the evening peak

questions.question: The closing frame of the whole unit assigns the roles:
options: Government builds, business votes, individuals legislate
Business writes the rules and government turns the bolts
Individuals write the roadmap for the utilities
Government writes the rules, business turns the heavy bolts, and sixty million households make the wave
